summary: Wired the previously test-only mypintusan (physical access control) logic and persistence layers into a runnable application for the first time: apps/mypintusan/app/app.go (the apphost.App composition root -- identity/local-admin seeding, login guard, RBAC role seeding, the SQLStore, the alarm sink routing door alarms into the shared notification feed, and the HTTP API), apps/mypintusan/app/runtime.go (supervises one OSDP bus per configured RS-485/TCP segment, re-dialling with 1s-30s backoff whenever the transport dies, and holds site lockdown state outside any single controller so a bus reconnect can never unseal a building), apps/mypintusan/apis (doors/readers, holders/credential issue-revoke, the read-only access log, lockdown, and the shared setup-wizard endpoints), apps/mypintusan/config + config.json (the site timezone -- required to parse, refuses to boot on a bad zone rather than silently falling back to UTC -- tick interval, PIN pairing window, and the RS-485 bus/reader list with per-reader SCBK), and cmd/mypintusan/main.go, now registered in the root -app launcher. Two production bugs were found and fixed by booting the binary against tools/osdp-sim, neither caught by any existing unit test: (1) infra/access/osdp/bus.go's Bus.Run polled a dead transport forever instead of returning when the port died (a USB-RS485 adapter unplugged, or a gateway reboot, silently killed every door on that segment until a process restart) -- fixed with a one-shot failPort/portErr signal that makes Run return so its owner can re-dial; (2) services.BusActuator was driving the OSDP PD address off Door.RelayChannel, which is actually the relay OUTPUT channel on that device, a different number -- a badge decision granted, the audit row said ok, and the door never opened; fixed by replacing BusActuator's separate Output/Address fields with a single StrikeResolver (services.SQLStore.StrikeFor), which resolves the PD address from the door's entry reader instead. Live-verified end to end against the simulator: 23 tables created, roles and the local admin seeded, the configured bus dialled, 191 granted badge events, a strike fired; the full HTTP surface (login, doors, readers, holders, events, unlock, lockdown) exercised; an operator remote-unlock lands in the same access log as a badge (raw_credential='operator'), and an unlock attempted during lockdown was refused and logged.
compatibility: There is still no frontend for this app -- API only, no views/static/SPA, no setup-wizard UI -- and it has no infra/versioning/version.json app manifest entry, so it stays scoped 'infra' here per this repo's version-bump rule (an app-named changelog scope hard-errors until its manifest entry exists) and is not yet part of the release/tagging pipeline; running it requires an operator to build/launch it explicitly (go run . -app mypintusan or cmd/mypintusan) and is not exposed through any existing installer. The infra/access/osdp/bus.go behavior change (Run now returns on a dead port instead of polling forever) is currently consumed only by mypintusan's new runtime supervisor; no other app uses this package, so no other product's behavior changes. Controller.ContactChanged (the myiotsan door-contact binding) remains an unwired seam, Door.RelayDeviceKey -> myiotsan CommandService.Issue actuation remains unimplemented, only tcp://host:port OSDP buses dial (serial transport is build-order step 5, not done), and there is no myseliasan fleet adoption (needs a new fleetnode node kind that does not exist yet). None of this affects any other shipping app in the suite.
